title: Relative associated points under arbitrary base change
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a locally finite type morphism of schemes [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], $\mathcal F$ a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module [pqf-def-coherent], and $g:S'\to S$ any morphism. Form $X'=X\times_SS'$ with projections $g':X'\to X$ and $f':X'\to S'$ [def-pc-base-change], and put $\mathcal F'=(g')^*\mathcal F$ [def-pc-module-pullback]. For a point $z\in X$ with $r=f(z)$, say $z\in\operatorname{Ass}_{X/S}(\mathcal F)$ if the maximal ideal of $\mathcal O_{X_r,z}$ is the annihilator of a nonzero element of $(\mathcal F_r)_z$ [def-weil-pbc-annihilator-associated-primes; def-weil-pbc-module-stalk], where $\mathcal F_r$ is the pullback to the fibre $X_r$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre]. Define $\operatorname{Ass}_{X'/S'}(\mathcal F')$ in the same way. If $z'\in X'$ maps to $z\in X$, $r'\in S'$ and $r\in S$, then $z'\in\operatorname{Ass}_{X'/S'}(\mathcal F')$ if and only if $z\in\operatorname{Ass}_{X/S}(\mathcal F)$ and $z'$ is a generic point [def-sc-generic-point] of an irreducible component [def-weil-irreducible-components] of the fibre over $z$ of $X'_{r'}\to X_r$, identified with $\operatorname{Spec}(\kappa(r')\otimes_{\kappa(r)}\kappa(z))$. Here residue fields are [def-weil-residue-field], $\operatorname{Spec}$ is [def-weil-affine-spectrum], and tensor products are [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] (for algebras the multiplication is $(a\otimes b)(c\otimes d)=ac\otimes bd$).

proof.text: Put $k=\kappa(r)$, $k'=\kappa(r')$, $Y=X_r$ and $Y'=X'_{r'}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-of-base-change] there is a cartesian square identifying $h:Y'\to Y$ with the base change of $\operatorname{Spec}k'\to\operatorname{Spec}k$. If $i:Y\to X$ and $i':Y'\to X'$ are the fibre projections, then $i\circ h=g'\circ i'$. Pullback composition in [def-pc-module-pullback] therefore gives $\mathcal F'_{r'}=(i')^*(g')^*\mathcal F\cong h^*i^*\mathcal F=h^*\mathcal F_r$. This comparison identifies the same pullback module, rather than changing the coefficient sheaf.

source.place: Tag 05DC, first paragraph: cartesian fibre square and coefficient pullback identification

proof.text: The map $\operatorname{Spec}k'\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is flat by [lem-pc-field-extension-flat]. Its base change $h$ is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-base-change]. No flatness of the original morphism $f$ or of $g$ is required.

source.place: Tag 05DC, first paragraph: flatness of the field-extension morphism of fibres

proof.text: The structure map $Y\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is locally of finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-lft-base-change]. A field has only the ideals $(0)$ and $(1)$, so its spectrum is locally Noetherian. Apply [pqf-lem-locnoeth-lft] to conclude that $Y$ is locally Noetherian. The sheaf $\mathcal F_r=i^*\mathcal F$ is quasi-coherent by [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-quasi-coherent]. Thus the flat pullback formula can be applied with base $Y$ and arbitrary quasi-coherent coefficients $\mathcal F_r$; no finite generation of $\mathcal F$ has been assumed.

source.place: Tag 05DC, first paragraph: locally Noetherian fibre and quasi-coherent coefficients

proof.text:
Apply [lem-trf-flat-pullback-associated-points] to $h:Y'\to Y$ and $\mathcal G=\mathcal F_r$, using steps 1–3. It gives
$$\operatorname{Ass}_{Y'}(\mathcal F'_{r'})=\bigcup_{y\in\operatorname{Ass}_Y(\mathcal F_r)}j_y\operatorname{Ass}_{Y'_y}(\mathcal O_{Y'_y}).$$
The point of $Y$ underlying $z'\in Y'$ is the canonical point $z\in X_r$. Since the images of the fibre maps $j_y$ lie over their respective $y$, this equality says precisely that $z'$ is associated to $\mathcal F'_{r'}$ if and only if $z$ is associated to $\mathcal F_r$ and the corresponding point of $Y'_z$ is associated to $\mathcal O_{Y'_z}$.

source.place: Tag 05DC, displayed associated-point formula and its interpretation at the given point

proof.text: The residue field at the canonical point $z\in Y=X_r$ is $\kappa(z)$: on affine charts, clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-ring-primes-residue-fields] identifies the residue field in the fibre ring with that of the original point. Base-changing the square of step 1 along $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(z)\to Y$, the fibre $Y'_z$ is consequently $\operatorname{Spec}k'\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(z)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] it is $\operatorname{Spec}T$ for $T=k'\otimes_k\kappa(z)$. To check the finiteness needed below, choose an affine neighbourhood $V=\operatorname{Spec}R$ of $r$ and a finite-type affine chart $U=\operatorname{Spec}B$ of $f^{-1}(V)$ containing $z$, as in [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-residue-field-extension-finitely-generated] to $R\to B$ and the primes of $r,z$. It gives that $\kappa(z)/k$ is finitely generated as a field, even when $z$ is not closed.

source.place: Tag 05DC, second paragraph: identify the residual fibre and verify the finite-type field hypothesis of 045M

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-tensor-fields-cohen-macaulay] to $k'/k$ and $\kappa(z)/k$, the latter finitely generated by step 5. Thus $T$ is Noetherian and every $T_{\mathfrak q}$ is Noetherian local Cohen–Macaulay. The other extension $k'/k$ may be completely arbitrary. We now determine the associated points of $\operatorname{Spec}T$ directly in these local rings.

source.place: Tag 05DC, second paragraph: apply the tensor-fields Cohen–Macaulay theorem

proof.text: Let $\mathfrak q\in\operatorname{Spec}T$ be an associated point of its structure sheaf. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization](c) its local ring is $T_{\mathfrak q}$; association means its maximal ideal $\mathfrak qT_{\mathfrak q}$ is an element-annihilator associated prime of that ring. Step 6 and [lem-weil-pbc-cm-local-associated-prime-minimal] imply that $\mathfrak qT_{\mathfrak q}$ is a minimal prime of $T_{\mathfrak q}$. The inclusion-preserving prime correspondence [lem-weil-pbc-primes-of-localization](1) now implies that $\mathfrak q$ is minimal in $T$: a strictly smaller prime would extend to a strictly smaller prime below $\mathfrak qT_{\mathfrak q}$, a contradiction.

source.place: Tag 05DC, second paragraph: Cohen–Macaulay local rings have no embedded associated primes

proof.text: Conversely, if $\mathfrak q$ is a minimal prime of $T$, the Noetherian hypothesis from step 6 lets us apply [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-minimal-prime-associated]: $\mathfrak q$ is an element-annihilator associated prime of $T$. By [lem-weil-pbc-associated-prime-localization-depth-zero], its extension $\mathfrak qT_{\mathfrak q}$ is associated to $T_{\mathfrak q}$. The stalk identification [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization](c) therefore says that $\mathfrak q$ is an associated point of the structure sheaf of $\operatorname{Spec}T$. Together with step 7 this characterizes those associated points as exactly the minimal primes.

source.place: Tag 05DC, second paragraph: minimal primes of a Noetherian ring are associated

proof.text: The prime-ideal/irreducible-closed-set correspondence in [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring] reverses inclusions: the closure of $\{\mathfrak q\}$ is $V(\mathfrak q)$, and it is a maximal irreducible closed subset exactly when $\mathfrak q$ is minimal. By [def-sc-generic-point] these are exactly the generic points of irreducible components of $\operatorname{Spec}T$. Hence steps 7–8 replace the last condition in step 4 by the generic-component condition of the statement. Finally the fibrewise definition [def-trf-relative-assassin] identifies association of $z$ to $\mathcal F_r$, respectively of $z'$ to $\mathcal F'_{r'}$, with membership in the two relative assassins. This proves both implications of the desired equivalence.

source.place: Tag 05DC, conclusion: minimal primes are component generic points and relative assassin is fibrewise association

proof_origin.place: Tag 05DC (lemma-base-change-relative-assassin), complete proof; no-embedded-points argument made local via the existing Cohen–Macaulay associated-prime lemma.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q19-a7cc8455c (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Read Divisors 05DC (lemma-base-change-relative-assassin), 05DB (lemma-bourbaki) and its input 05C2, and Algebra 045M (lemma-tensor-fields-CM, whose proof via 045I uses finitely generated field extensions), all in full; the tags are verified in tags/tags. The item states 05DC exactly: f locally of finite type, F arbitrary quasi-coherent, g arbitrary, fibrewise association by element annihilators, and the generic-component condition on Spec(κ(r')⊗κ(z)). The parent's steps 3 and 7 use it in exactly this form. Steps 1–9 each say what their cited statements say. (1) fibre square and pullback composition give F'_{r'}≅h^*F_r. (2) field-extension flatness plus flat base change make h flat. (3) the fibre is locally Noetherian because it is locally of finite type over a field, and F_r is quasi-coherent; S need not be Noetherian. (4) the flat-pullback formula at z' uses that fibre images lie over their indexing point. (5) the residue field is unchanged on fibre-ring charts, and κ(z)/κ(r) is finitely generated by a finite-type chart, with z not necessarily closed. (6) 045M needs only one extension finitely generated. (7) the CM local lemma (depth≥dim) plus the localization prime bijection give associated ⇒ minimal. (8) for a Noetherian ring, minimal primes are associated, and association passes to the localization. (9) V(q) gives minimal primes = component generic points. `uses` equals the cited ids and `proof_deps` is their union. Both new nodes are true, self-contained, statement-only and searched. Small cases tested: k(t)⊗k(u) (the diagonal prime is not associated, so the generic-component condition is needed); K⊗K=K[ε]/(ε^p) (not reduced, but CM); non-finitely-generated extensions (Noetherianity fails, so the hypothesis is needed); Z[x]/Z with G=O and G=Z/p. Neither new node duplicates an existing one: 0312 lem-weil-pbc-associated-primes-flat-base-change is ring-level, 05C2 lem-trf-associated-primes-fibre-bound needs finite modules and gives one inclusion, and lem-pur-cohen-macaulay-field-extension is only for schemes locally of finite type. Neither restates the item. Accepted tool_uses: lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-quasi-coherent, lem-weil-pbc-fibre-ring-primes-residue-fields and lem-weil-pbc-cm-local-associated-prime-minimal, all generic sk-thm-p1 facts; every other off-unit citation is a Mathlib leaf. No SGA. Not a target node. lean.statement: theorem relativeAssassin_baseChange_iff {X S S' : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) [LocallyOfFiniteType f] (F : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent] (g : S' ⟶ S) (z' : ↑(Limits.pullback f g)) : z' ∈ relativeAssassin (Limits.pullback.snd f g) ((tensorPullback (Limits.pullback.fst f g)).obj F) ↔ Limits.pullback.fst f g z' ∈ relativeAssassin f F ∧ ∃ Z ∈ irreducibleComponents (Spec (Scheme.Pullback.Triplet.ofPoint ((pullbackSymmetry f g).hom z')).tensor), IsGenericPoint (Scheme.Pullback.SpecOfPoint ((pullbackSymmetry f g).hom z')) Z
